authenticity_review: The image is a stylized cartoon illustration. While the style is consistent, there are notable structural artifacts that reduce authenticity: (1) Elephant feet merge into the ground plane without clear toe definition or proper grounding shadows (melting effect), particularly visible on the leftmost and middle elephants. (2) The legs of the middle elephants show slight spatial fusion/overlap where they should be distinct. (3) The animal_pose_auditor flagged low-confidence keypoints in face and limb regions for multiple instances, correlating with these structural ambiguities. The lion is well-rendered with good anatomical fidelity for the style, but the elephant structural issues are significant enough to warrant a moderate penalty. The missing fourth elephant is an alignment issue, not an authenticity artifact per se, but the rendering quality of the existing elephants is compromised.
key_defects: Missing one elephant (count is 3 instead of 4) - critical alignment failure
Elephant feet merge into ground plane without clear definition (structural grounding failure)
Slight fusion between middle elephant legs indicating spatial inconsistency
Low-confidence pose keypoints in elephant face and limb regions correlate with structural ambiguity
Cartoon style inherently lacks specific Indian elephant taxonomy features (twin-domed skull, single trunk finger, toenails)
